S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report to the relevant regulator every fire, thermal runaway, or overheating event involving a battery, including events without injury, property damage, or emergency-service response. Initial notice is due within 24 hours of learning of the event; a preliminary investigation report is due within 10 business days, with material updates provided promptly. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 72 hours when an incident reveals a credible product safety risk, providing safety instructions and updates as the investigation proceeds.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each battery model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C before market entry and at least annually thereafter, using a regulator-approved protocol and independent laboratory. A model with a failure rate above 5% must submit a corrective-action plan and be retested within 12 months. Exceeding 5% alone does not automatically prohibit sales; regulators may restrict new sales or require further safeguards if the model remains above the limit after retesting.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: For installed systems lacking this capability, manufacturers must provide a safe retrofit or equivalent risk-reduction measure within 6 years of adoption, prioritizing systems with known safety risks.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery systems must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer must immediately notify the regulator and initiate an independent review, while providing affected customers with interim safety information. A recall or other corrective action must be required when the review confirms an unacceptable safety risk; regulators may order a recall at any time where evidence shows an imminent serious risk, regardless of the rate.

document.section_notes: S1 is the strongest section: all thermal events must be reported within 24 hours with customer notice at 72 hours. The final text removes the numeric recall trigger, so exceeding 8 per 100,000 leads to review rather than a mandatory recall, and S2 allows above-5% models to keep selling indefinitely. Per-model results go to purchasers and regulators but are not published, and S3 and S4 fall within the acceptable ranges, with a 6-year retrofit and 36-month suppression requirement.
